title: Into the Eagle's Nest
build: PAL cassette, Pandora 1987, analysed at the loader's hand-over

tools.host: Linux 6.6 x86_64 (WSL2) on Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Ubuntu 26.04, display through WSLg
tools.emulator: own build of github.com/barryw/vice-mcp, release v3.13.2, commit 1e83aab134; driven through kit/c64/vice.py; check-emulator 57 of 57

exclude: runtime: the screen, which the game fills with tiles and the status panel; the bytes the loader left here are its own loading screen
runtime: the sprite pointers and the bytes beside them, written at the start of every mission
runtime: the figures' positions on the floor, filled in by the map builder at $6A40 as it reads the floor's description
runtime: the figures' places in the castle map and their kinds, filled in by the map builder
runtime: the 256 random bytes $67CA reads out of the sound chip's noise oscillator at start-up
runtime: the buffer the message printer at $5935 fills with the characters of the line being shown
runtime: untouched at the hand-over, inside the map builder's working area
runtime: the top quarter of the castle map, built from the floor's description by $6A40
runtime: the bottom part of the castle map, built from the floor's description by $6A40
extra: the title picture's bitmap, loaded from tape and shown while the rest of the tape loads; the castle map is built over it once the game runs
include: the four floors' descriptions, a kilobyte each, which the game reads with the I/O area banked out
